subject.title: fix(launcher): stop respawned children after parent death on Unix

question: After this branch is refreshed, is targeted Ubuntu launcher SIGKILL proof enough to land the parent-death guard, or should exact Linux systemd/root-owned gateway restart proof be required first?
rationale: The patch changes launcher supervision and the exact reported service-manager scenario was not rerun, so automation should not decide the final proof bar for an availability-sensitive startup path.

options.title: Land after refresh and focused checks
options.body: Resolve the conflicts, rerun the focused launcher/process tests and formatting checks, and land the parent-death guard if the refreshed diff still matches this shape.

options.title: Require exact systemd proof
options.body: Ask for Linux systemd restart proof that kills or crashes the wrapper and verifies the gateway port is released before merge.

options.title: Pause for a different mitigation
options.body: Hold this PR if maintainers prefer a systemd-unit or stale-port cleanup approach instead of child-side parent-death detection.

recommendation.title: Land after refresh and focused checks
recommendation.body: Resolve the conflicts, rerun the focused launcher/process tests and formatting checks, and land the parent-death guard if the refreshed diff still matches this shape.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history and current blame put the respawn runner and launcher supervision path closest to this owner signal.
